title: Verifier-Guided Repair of LLM-Generated Vendor CLI Configurations: A Controlled Fault-Injection Paired Study
abstract: We evaluate whether exposing deterministic verifier diagnostics to an LLM-based repair workflow reduces residual unsafe or invalid vendor-CLI configurations compared with blind repair. In a preregistered controlled-challenge paired design (vCLI_fault_injection_repair_2026_A_prereg_v1) using adapter hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2 and shared controlled-fault candidates, we planned 40 confirmatory pairs and observed 39 complete pairs (one source generation invalid and excluded per preregistered rules). Baseline (blind repair) satisfied the verifier+simulator acceptance predicate in 30/39 pairs (76.92%); guarded (verifier-guided) satisfied it in 38/39 pairs (97.44%). Paired counts: n11 = 29, n10 = 9 (guarded-only), n01 = 1 (baseline-only), n00 = 0. The paired absolute difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.20512820512820507 (20.51 percentage points); two-sided exact paired test p = 0.021484375; 95% paired-bootstrap percentile CI = [0.07692307692307693, 0.358974358974359] (bootstrap resamples = 10000, seed = 1729). Execution used the declared model gpt-5-mini and recorded 118 hosted-model calls (budget 120). A preregistered confirmatory harmful-overrepair aggregation was not produced by the archived confirmatory executor; the preregistered harmful-change mapping and all per-episode traces required to compute it are archived and their locations are documented in Methods. We present the confirmatory result, document the reproducibility path for the unresolved preregistered safety aggregation, and discuss operational implications and threats to validity.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed as aids in network operations (NetOps) for tasks such as intent-to-configuration translation and automated remediation. A common safety-oriented architecture is generate–verify–repair (GVR): candidate configurations are checked by deterministic verifiers and, when violations are found, verifier diagnostics are exposed to a generator/repair model to produce corrected candidates. Prior empirical work in code and Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC) settings reports that interposing deterministic verifiers can raise verifier-detected pass rates while exposing new failure modes (e.g., verifier-exploitation) and imposing interaction costs [1]–[3]. Field and survey studies of LLMs in NetOps/AIOps warn that read-oriented assistance does not straightforwardly imply safe closed-loop autonomous changes [4].

Motivation and research question. Controlled paired evidence on verifier-guided repair applied to vendor command-line interface (CLI) templates with preregistered realistic fault operators is sparse, and intervention informativeness is a known methodological pitfall: a verifier-guided intervention can affect outcomes only when initial candidates trigger actionable diagnostics. We address this by running a preregistered deterministic controlled-fault injection and a paired design that shares the same controlled-fault candidate across arms. Research question: Does exposing deterministic verifier diagnostics to an LLM repair workflow reduce residual unsafe or invalid vendor-CLI configurations compared with blind repair when confronted with preregistered controlled faults?
sections.related_work: Empirical GVR evidence in adjacent domains supports the utility of deterministic diagnostics as repair signals while documenting important caveats. Work on generate–verify–repair for code and DSLs reports increased verifier pass rates when diagnostics are used by repair models (e.g., program/patch repair and IaC evaluations) [1], [2]. Controlled analyses have shown that iterative refinement toward a single verifier can produce pathological 'verifier-exploitation' behaviors; mitigation strategies are proposed but not universally validated [3]. Studies instrumenting verifier-mediated agent pipelines quantify a measurable verifier-induced interaction cost (a "verifier tax") that affects latency and compute budgets [4]. Surveys and field case studies focusing on NetOps/AIOps emphasize that LLMs are often useful for read-oriented tasks but that closed-loop configuration changes require cautious verification and governance [5]. (Citation mapping: [1] supports GVR efficacy in program/IaC benchmarks; [2] demonstrates verifier-guided improvements on infrastructure templates; [3] analyzes verifier-exploitation risks; [4] measures verifier-mediated interaction costs; [5] reports NetOps survey/case-study qualifications.)
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The study was preregistered as vCLI_fault_injection_repair_2026_A_prereg_v1. Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline, where a binary success requires both the deterministic vendor-CLI verifier and a simulator-based compliance agreement. The preregistration SHA-256 is recorded in the execution manifest (preregistration_sha256 = 0ba66573928647f008b2cd5b9dde6708a61ae86ece55b693ace534e01e2b132c).

Design and adapter semantics. Confirmatory execution used adapter hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2 under its shared_controlled_fault_candidate semantics: for each preregistered task index a single deterministically injected controlled-fault candidate was produced and reused unchanged across both conditions. Each pair received exactly one initial generation (shared) and one repair opportunity per condition; baseline denotes blind repair (no verifier diagnostics exposed) and guarded denotes repair with deterministic validator diagnostics exposed. The adapter-mandated confirmatory task_count was fixed at 40. The declared model for confirmatory execution is gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json). The archived model configuration records temperature = null (unset); null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0.

Runtime sampling records and reproducibility pointer (reviewer request). Runtime sampling parameters and per-call provider traces are archived for every hosted-model call. Auditors and reproducers can find per-call provider traces and sampling metadata at execution/provider_calls/*.json (per-call request/response traces) and the global declared model settings at execution/model_configuration.json; execution/execution_log.jsonl contains timestamps and call-level events. The execution manifest and provider_call_audit entries also summarize model_call totals (hosted_model_call_event_count = 118). These archived artifacts contain the runtime sampling parameters recorded for each hosted-model call; the presence of temperature = null in execution/model_configuration.json should not be interpreted as temperature = 0 or deterministic sampling.

Controlled-challenge sampling and informativeness. To ensure intervention activation we preregistered deterministic controlled faults (task indices 1..40) that inject realistic actionable violations (examples: missing required restore, protected-interface change). The execution manifest records controlled_fault_assignment_sha256 = 8d0879872348ae94a45f3d674df57d6552624cd841b62ab239a280347f5275c6 and source_generation_attempt_count = 40 (source_valid_count = 39, source_invalid_or_failed_count = 1). The preregistered missingness rule 'complete_pair_primary' excludes a pair only if both condition executions are unscorable; this occurred once and is documented in analysis/missingness_summary.csv.

Scoring and preregistered harmful-change mapping. The primary success predicate required both the deterministic vendor-CLI validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) and simulator-based compliance agreement. The preregistration froze a harmful-change labeling schema used for a preregistered harmful-overrepair hypothesis: the archived scoring pipeline labels an episode harmful if validation_after.violation_codes contains PROTECTED_INTERFACE_CHANGE or UNINTENDED_STATE_CHANGE. The transformation artifact implementing this mapping is archived at execution/transformation_manifest.json and per-episode validator traces are archived at execution/scoring/*.json and execution/raw_results.jsonl.

Statistical analysis plan. The preregistered primary test is an exact paired binary test (two-sided McNemar exact or equivalent exact paired binomial), reporting absolute paired risk difference, discordant-pair counts, exact two-sided p-value, and a 95% paired-bootstrap percentile CI (bootstrap resamples = 10000, seed = 1729). The preregistration defined a single primary confirmatory test (no multiplicity correction) and labeled subgroup/per-fault-class analyses exploratory. Missingness sensitivity analyses were preregistered: (1) primary analysis excludes incomplete pairs per 'complete_pair_primary'; (2) a sensitivity analysis treats missing episodes as failures. All per-episode raw artifacts and provider traces required to recompute any preregistered aggregation are archived at the listed artifact locations.
sections.results:
Execution accounting. Planned confirmatory pairs = 40; completed episodes = 78 (39 complete pairs) with failed_episode_count = 2 and source_valid_count = 39 (one source invalid). Hosted-model calls used = 118 (<= maximum 120). Run timestamps are recorded in the execution manifest (started_at_utc = 2026-09-04T21:16:50.730326+00:00; completed_at_utc = 2026-09-04T21:19:34.370550+00:00). Stage-level counts are archived in the provider_call_audit (valid_source_generation = 40; blind_controlled_fault_repair = 39; validator_guided_controlled_fault_repair = 39).

Primary confirmatory outcomes (complete_pairs = 39). Baseline (blind repair) success = 30/39 = 0.7692307692307693. Guarded (verifier-guided) success = 38/39 = 0.9743589743589743. Paired contingency counts (guarded, baseline): n11 = 29, n10 = 9 (guarded-only), n01 = 1 (baseline-only), n00 = 0. Paired estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.20512820512820507 (20.51 percentage points). Exact two-sided paired test (McNemar exact): p = 0.021484375. 95% paired-bootstrap percentile CI = [0.07692307692307693, 0.358974358974359] (bootstrap_resamples = 10000, bootstrap_seed = 1729). The archived analysis outputs analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv and analysis/condition_summary.csv contain the same counts and are recorded in the artifact manifest.

Missingness and excluded pair. One pair was excluded under the preregistered 'complete_pair_primary' rule because its source-generation was invalid/unscorable (both_missing_pairs = 1). Per-episode terminal error reasons and logs are archived at execution/execution_log.jsonl and execution/raw_results.jsonl.

Preregistered harmful-overrepair aggregation: status and reproducibility path. The preregistration included a confirmatory safety hypothesis bounding harmful-overrepair. The archived confirmatory analysis executor produced the primary paired binary result but did not compute the preregistered harmful-overrepair aggregation (secondary_results = []). Because the confirmatory summary omitted that aggregation, we do not present a retroactive preregistered confirmatory safety claim here. To enable exact independent reproduction of the preregistered harmful-overrepair aggregation auditors should: (1) iterate the preregistered complete pairs (analysis/missingness_summary.csv shows complete_pairs = 39), (2) for each pair read validation_after.violation_codes from execution/scoring/<episode>.json (or execution/raw_results.jsonl), (3) label an episode harmful if validation_after.violation_codes contains PROTECTED_INTERFACE_CHANGE or UNINTENDED_STATE_CHANGE (the frozen mapping archived at execution/transformation_manifest.json), and (4) compute paired harmful counts and the paired difference per the preregistered analysis plan. All required per-episode fields and the transformation artifact are present in the archived evidence bundle; the archived confirmatory executor did not run this aggregation and therefore the preregistered harmful-overrepair claim remains unresolved in this paper.

Representative diagnostics. Representative per-pair scoring artifacts are archived (execution/scoring/task-000001-*.json, task-000002-*.json, task-000003-*.json). For example, pair-000001 exhibits fault_class = dropped_required_restore and both arms produced valid repairs; pair-000003 exhibits a protected-interface change where baseline repair left PROTECTED_INTERFACE_CHANGE violations while guarded repair removed those violations and yielded a valid configuration. These per-episode traces support a mechanism in which diagnostics direct targeted corrective edits.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation and mechanism. The preregistered paired result shows a substantial increase in verifier+simulator-validated success when deterministic verifier diagnostics are exposed to the repair model under shared controlled-fault pairing semantics. The shared-candidate pairing semantics isolate the effect of exposing diagnostics because both arms received the same initial controlled-fault candidate and repair budgets; differences therefore arise from the presence or absence of deterministic diagnostics during repair. Archived per-episode traces show diagnostics identifying specific violation codes that the guarded condition uses to generate targeted corrective edits, providing a plausible causal pathway for the observed gains.

Operational considerations and verifier tax. The guarded workflow incurs measurable interaction steps: execution used 118 hosted-model calls and stage counts document each pipeline phase. These instrumented counts permit exploratory computation of model-call cost per avoided failure, but the present confirmatory run does not generalize cost/latency to production scale. Practitioners should budget for verifier-mediated call counts, validate verifier coverage for critical safety properties, and enforce harmful-change constraints (for example via mappings like the preregistered harmful-change rules) before deploying closed-loop changes.

Safety boundary and unresolved safety aggregation. Importantly, the preregistered confirmatory harmful-overrepair aggregation was not present in the archived confirmatory summary; we therefore treat that preregistered safety verdict as unresolved while providing the exact archived inputs and mapping needed for independent recomputation. This preserves the preregistration audit trail and avoids retroactive confirmatory claims.

Threats to validity. Internal validity: recorded model temperature = null (unset) and exactly-one sampled initial generation per pair limit claims about deterministic sampling; per-call sampling metadata are archived at execution/provider_calls/*.json and execution/model_configuration.json. Construct validity: primary success requires agreement of verifier and simulator; simulator fidelity constrains the operational meaning of "valid." External validity: a single declared model (gpt-5-mini) and a synthetic controlled-fault bank constrain generalization to diverse vendor equipment and live operator streams. Conclusion validity: complete_pairs = 39 provides reasonable precision for the observed effect but limits fine-grained subgroup inference.
sections.conclusion: In a preregistered controlled-challenge paired experiment using hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2 and shared controlled-fault candidates, exposing deterministic verifier diagnostics to an LLM repair workflow produced a statistically detectable and substantial increase in verifier+simulator-validated configuration success (≈ +20.51 percentage points; p = 0.021484375; 95% CI [0.07692307692307693, 0.358974358974359]). This result is bounded to the preregistered synthetic task bank, the declared model (gpt-5-mini), and the archived deterministic verifier and simulator. The preregistered confirmatory harmful-overrepair aggregation was not computed by the archived confirmatory executor and therefore remains unresolved for the confirmatory claim; the transformation artifact and per-episode traces required to compute it are archived and the exact reproduction path is documented in Methods. We release the artifact bundle for reproducible reaggregation and recommend multi-model, multi-verifier replications and larger-scale cost/latency studies to evaluate operational feasibility and safety at NetOps scale.

disclosure_statement: Preregistration: vCLI_fault_injection_repair_2026_A_prereg_v1 (preregistration_sha256 recorded in the execution manifest). Adapter: hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2. Declared model used for confirmatory execution: gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json). Exact initial master prompt archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256: f781dd7978328198146d586cf33e0f4b783c8db126bd0f16fcd13699455ebb10). Human role: a Research Director selected the topic family and pre-lock constraints; after the autonomy lock the autonomous system performed literature verification, preregistration, experiment execution, analysis, and manuscript generation; no manual human editing of technical manuscript content occurred after the lock. Execution semantics: execution manifest records temperature = null/unset in execution/model_configuration.json; null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0. Per-call provider traces and runtime sampling parameters are archived at execution/provider_calls/*.json and the global model settings at execution/model_configuration.json; timestamps and call-level events are in execution/execution_log.jsonl. Pairing semantics: exactly one sampled initial generation per task pair was performed and reused by both arms under shared_controlled_fault_candidate semantics; baseline denotes blind repair and guarded denotes repair with deterministic validator diagnostics exposed. The preregistered harmful-change mapping is archived (execution/transformation_manifest.json) and per-episode traces required to reproduce preregistered safety aggregations are archived at execution/raw_results.jsonl and execution/scoring/*.json. The study followed the preregistered stopping rule; no silent adapter substitution occurred.
limitations: Synthetic controlled-fault task bank: tasks were deterministically injected and do not represent a broad naturalistic distribution of production NetOps incidents; external validity to live operator workloads is limited.
Single-model and single-adapter evaluation: confirmatory execution used only the declared model gpt-5-mini and one adapter family; results do not establish multi-model generality.
Simulator-backed primary success predicate: primary success required agreement of deterministic verifier and simulator; simulator fidelity and verifier coverage constrain construct validity.

Sample size and power: complete_pairs = 39 provides detectable effects of the observed magnitude but limits precision for subgroup and per-fault-class inference; exploratory subgroup analyses are not confirmatory.
Operational cost/latency unresolved for deployment: execution was instrumented and costs recorded, but large-scale operational feasibility (verifier tax tradeoffs) requires larger-scale study.

Verifier-exploitation and long-horizon agentic pathologies remain possible: this controlled setting mitigates some risks, but broader agentic workflows need additional defenses (multi-verifier designs, calibrated abstention, uncertainty quantification).

Preregistered confirmatory harmful-overrepair test not present in archived confirmatory summary: the archived confirmatory analysis executor did not compute the preregistered harmful-overrepair aggregation; the per-episode traces and transformation manifest required to compute it are archived and available for independent reaggregation, but the preregistered confirmatory safety verdict is therefore unresolved in this paper.
